# Sirach Chapter 46 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 46 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 46 covers Joshua (vv. 1–6), Caleb and the Judges (vv. 7–12), and Samuel (vv. 13–20). The chapter ends with the extraordinary statement (v. 20) that Samuel prophesied even after death — a reference to 1 Samuel 28, the witch of Endor episode, treated here without embarrassment as genuine prophecy.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 1: "as his name declared" — Yehoshua/Joshua = "YHWH saves/is salvation." Preserve the name-etymology note.
- v. 4: "the sun stood still" — Joshua 10:12–13. "One day became as two days" — preserve the specific formulation.
- v. 7: "work of mercy" (EMET) vs. "deed of loyal love" (LOGOS) — Greek ergon eleous = work of lovingkindness. "Loyal love" (LOGOS) echoes hesed; "mercy" (EMET) is more common English. SOPHIA adopts "deed of faithful loyalty."
- v. 11: "play the harlot" (EMET) vs. "turn to idolatry" — Greek eporneusan = committed fornication/played the harlot. In context this is spiritual fornication = idolatry. EMET preserves the metaphor; LOGOS interprets.
- v. 19: "pair of sandals" — echoes 1 Sam. 12:3 and Amos 2:6.
- v. 20: "even after he had fallen asleep he prophesied" — SOPHIA preserves this as the climactic statement of Samuel's greatness. It must not be hedged.

---

**46:1** Joshua son of Nun was mighty in war and was the successor of Moses in the prophetic office; he was, as his name declares, a great salvation for his people — appointed for vengeance on the enemies that rose against them — so that he might give Israel its inheritance.

**46:2** How glorious he was when he lifted up his hand and brandished his sword against the cities!

**46:3** Who before him had stood so firm? For he himself fought the wars of the Lord.

**46:4** Was it not by his hand that the sun stood still, so that one day became as long as two?

**46:5** He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when enemies pressed him hard on every side; and the great Lord answered him with hailstones of overpowering force.

**46:6** He overwhelmed a nation in battle, and on the descent he utterly destroyed his opponents, so that the nations might know his armament — that he was fighting in the presence of the Lord, following the Mighty One.

**46:7** And in the days of Moses also he performed a work of faithful loyalty — he and Caleb son of Jephunneh — in standing firm against the congregation, in restraining the people from sin, and in silencing their wicked murmuring.

**46:8** Of six hundred thousand infantry, those two alone were preserved to bring them into their inheritance, into a land flowing with milk and honey.

**46:9** And the Lord gave Caleb strength, and strength remained with him to old age, so that he went up to the hill country of the land, and his descendants received it as their inheritance,

**46:10** so that all the children of Israel might see how good it is to follow the Lord.

**46:11** And the judges also — each one by name — all those whose hearts did not play the harlot and who did not turn away from the Lord — may their memory be blessed!

**46:12** May their bones sprout anew from where they lie, and may the honored name of those men live again in their sons.

**46:13** Samuel was beloved of the Lord; a prophet of the Lord, he established the kingdom and anointed rulers over his people.

**46:14** By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord kept watch over Jacob.

**46:15** By his faithfulness he was attested as a prophet, and by his words he was trusted as a seer.

**46:16** He called upon the Mighty Lord when enemies pressed him in on every side, as he offered a suckling lamb as a sacrifice.

**46:17** And the Lord thundered from heaven and made his great voice heard with a mighty crash.

**46:18** He crushed the commanders of the enemy and destroyed all the rulers of the Philistines.

**46:19** Before the time of his eternal sleep, he bore witness before the Lord and his anointed: "I have not taken anyone's property, not so much as a pair of sandals" — and no man accused him.

**46:20** And even after he had fallen asleep, he prophesied; he revealed to the king his impending death, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the wickedness of the people.
